- Use case: real-time personalized recommendations + short-form summarization for user inboxes (~2k users per day).
- Estimated traffic: ~250M tokens/month (peak), ~60M tokens/month (expected steady state).
- Goals: stay within a predictable unit cost (target $/1M tokens) while keeping median latency <= 150ms for 1kB prompts.

Next steps I promised on the call:
1) Share a simple price benchmark vs OpenAI/Anthropic/hosted open-model providers (attached).
2) Provide a sample cost projection for 60M vs 250M tokens/month with Redwood Dedicated and Hosted options.
3) Draft a short SOW outline to start procurement conversations.

Attached: Redwood-pricing-grid.xlsx (simple $/1M breakdown across model families + quantized variants).

Question for you — what is the target $/1M tokens you need to land to make this viable for the next 12 months? If you share a budget range, we can tailor a commitment/discount structure and identify whether Dedicated makes sense.

I'll loop in Vanessa on the economics/commitment side.

Best,

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up — pricing and benchmarking details

Sam —

Thanks for the quick answers, that's very helpful. Short answers below; attached is an annotated copy of the pricing grid with callouts for the specific volumes you mentioned.

- Network egress: typically billed separately by cloud provider; our Hosted price examples exclude cloud egress. For Dedicated / Private we can model egress if you want (depends on deployment topology).
- Discount tiers: 6-month commit typically starts at ~10% off list for volume commitments; 12-month and >$X/month commitments move to 20–35% depending on model family and whether you use Dedicated reserved capacity. We'll propose specific tiers once you confirm an initial commitment band.

Benchmark summary (high level, $ per 1M tokens):
- Redwood (hosted, open-model family, quantized): ~$420 / 1M tokens (standard) — can get to ~$300 / 1M with 12-month Reserved Dedicated pricing and model quantization.
- OpenAI (gpt-family comparable): ~ $1,200 / 1M tokens (current public list and customer examples).
- Anthropic (claude-family comparable): ~ $900 — $1,100 / 1M tokens depending on context window and usage patterns.
- Other open-model hosts (competitors): wide range — typical $350 — $800 / 1M depending on optimization and commitment.

So at 60M tokens/mo, switching to Redwood Dedicated with a 12-month commit could move your unit cost into the low-mid $300s / 1M tokens, which seems in-range of your target. At 250M tokens/mo, further volume discounts and potential batching/kv-caching optimizations can push effective cost closer to $250 — $300 / 1M in some cases.

Attached: annotated Redwood-pricing-grid.xlsx; SOW-draft.pdf (initial commercial terms).

Would you be open to a short pricing-ops call this week with Vanessa to walk through commitment bands and deployment options? I can bring a simple projection for 3 commitment tiers (monthly/6mo/12mo) and show latency/availability tradeoffs for Hosted vs Dedicated.

Thanks,
Rachel

Hi Sam —

Thanks for the details. Quick operational notes from the commercial side:

- If Acme can commit to a 12-month Reserved Dedicated contract at an expected average of 75–100M tokens/month, we can offer a blended unit price of $320 / 1M tokens (model family: quantized open-models), with a 30% off list cap on larger custom optimizations.
- For pure Hosted usage with no commitment we can provide a volume-based pricing table in the spreadsheet; the Hosted list sits higher (~$420 / 1M) but with easier onboarding and no infra commitments.
- We will exclude cloud egress from the table (will add a note). If you need us to build a fully loaded TCO for procurement, we'll coordinate with your infra team and the cloud account owner.

Next steps:
1) Sam/Priya — confirm a target commitment band (e.g., 6mo @ 60M avg, 12mo @ 75M avg, or 12mo @ 100M avg).
2) Rachel — prepare the 3-tier pricing projection + short SOW and send DocuSign-ready commercial terms.
3) Optional: schedule a 30-min follow-up ops call to walk through technical deployment differences (Hosted vs Dedicated).

Sam — happy to jump on a call tomorrow if that helps — what time works for you?

Best,
